validity.recommendation: Do not treat as confirmed. Re-verify against a primary source that specifically names a 'Gamasa-Edku' (or Gamasa-Idku) 121 km / 42in line before staging any further work on this row; if none surfaces, escalate for possible retraction.
validity.researcher_notes: TEST APPLIED: read the row's sole cited source directly (WebFetch), then searched independently in Arabic and English for a real 'Gamasa-Edku' pipeline; this is NOT the EGAS-2018-map-visual-ID situation (that defense applies to NA's Oct/Nov-2025-added P8050-8059 rows, not this one) because the row's own ref is a 2025 magazine and I fetched and read it directly rather than relying on a text-search miss against a map document. FINDING 1 - the cited source fails on its face: the current ref (https://petro-mag.org/ar/Magazine/v?id=b505c5e8-6d88-447d-959d-270acf864417), which is the SOLE citation stapled to every one of this row's seven ref units (Status/Fuel/PipelineType/Proposal/Length/Diameter/Location), is the table-of-contents/cover page of the November 2025 issue of an Egyptian petroleum trade magazine. Reading it directly: it names no pipeline called Gamasa, Edku, or Idku anywhere; its only pipeline-adjacent content is a generic feature blurb 'Petroleum pipelines .. an essential component in transporting and trading crude oil and petroleum products' (p.74 TOC listing). The url_verifier 'expected content present' passes recorded in the worklist for Length/Diameter/Proposal/Location are false positives - they matched on bare numeral/year tokens (e.g. '2025', '42', '121') that occur incidentally elsewhere on a busy magazine cover/TOC page, not on any statement about this pipeline. This is exactly the 'generic/aggregate citation that does not actually name this pipeline' failure mode the brief calls an existence flag in its own right, and the Status check already caught it independently ('200 but data value not found'). FINDING 2 - no independent source fills the gap: extensive Arabic-language search ('جمصة' 'إدكو' خط أنابيب غاز, variants with 'ادكو', with '121 كم') and English search turned up zero mentions, anywhere, of a Gamasa-Edku/Idku gas pipeline at 121 km / 42in. What DOES exist under the 'Gamasa' name is a different, real, already-documented project: 'خط غاز جمصة - فينوسا' (Gamasa-Fenosa/Veunsa gas line), 42in diameter, 34 km, cost 397 million EGP, built to feed the West Damietta power station from the Union Fenosa/SEGAS Damietta LNG complex - confirmed via Egypt's official Presidency projects portal (presidency.eg, title 'انشاء خط غاز جمصة - فينوسا') and independently corroborated by petro-news.com's '39 مشاريع' national gas-projects map article, which lists it as project #29 with the same 42in/34km/397M-EGP figures. This project is ALREADY in GEM under a different ProjectID: P6035 'Gamasa-Veunsa Gas Pipeline', status=operating, StartYear1=2015, LengthKnown=34 km, Diameter=42in (confirmed directly in the fresh GGIT gas snapshot) - and gem.wiki's own page for it (read for leads only, not cited) cites Al-Youm Al-Sabea, 2016-02-26, reporting the line supplying 6.8 million m3/day of gas to the West Damietta power station. P8010 shares P6035's origin town (Gamasa) and its exact diameter (42in) but swaps the well-documented destination 'Veunsa/Fenosa' for 'Edku' - a place roughly 90 km further west that no source connects to Gamasa - and roughly triples the length (121 km vs 34 km) with status flipped to proposed. I cannot rule out that a genuine, separate 121 km Gamasa-to-Edku trunk exists and is simply undocumented online, but given (a) the row's own citation does not support it at all, (b) no independent source of any kind names it, and (c) a real, sourced, differently-specified pipeline sharing the same distinctive origin name and diameter is already in GEM under a different PID, the more defensible reading is that this row is unsupported as recorded. SECONDARY NOTE (roster comparison, P8027): Edku and Idku are the same Arabic town (إدكو, Beheira governorate) - Arabic sources use both English spellings interchangeably for it (e.g. the Idku LNG plant is rendered 'Edku'/'Idku' across sources I pulled). P8027 'Damietta-Idku Gas Pipeline' (Damietta -> Beheira/Idku, 165 km, 32in) shares P8010's Edku/Idku endpoint, and Damietta sits only ~25-30 km from Gamasa along the same coastal corridor, so 165 km (from Damietta) vs 121 km (from Gamasa) is roughly the geometrically-consistent difference - i.e. these two rows COULD be describing overlapping or the same corridor measured from different start points. However the diameters differ (42in vs 32in), which per the standing heuristic (different diameter = usually two real parallel lines, not a duplicate) argues against a clean duplicate call; I did not find a source for P8027 either in this pass, so I am flagging the overlap as an open question for whoever reviews both rows together, not concluding a merge. Given P8010's total lack of independent support, resolving it likely does not turn on P8027 at all.

validity.researcher_notes: P6035 and P8010 both originate at 'Gamasa' and both carry 42in diameter, which is enough of a coincidence to warrant a side-by-side human review, but the two rows disagree on destination (Veunsa/Fenosa vs Edku), length (34 km vs 121 km) and status (operating vs proposed) - differences too large to call this a confirmed duplicate outright. Recorded here as a flag, not a merge recommendation, since I found zero support for the P8010 variant existing as its own asset (see the existence finding above) - the more likely outcome on review is that P8010 should be retracted/corrected rather than merged into P6035, but that determination needs a source I could not locate in this pass.

summary: P8010 (Gamasa-Edku, 121km, proposed) flagged as an EXISTENCE concern - its sole cited ref is a Nov-2025 magazine TOC page that names neither Gamasa nor Edku, and no independent Arabic or English source describes a Gamasa-Edku pipeline at all; the only real, sourced 'Gamasa' project found is the unrelated P6035 'Gamasa-Veunsa Gas Pipeline' (34km, operating, already in GEM under a different PID) - flagged secondarily as a possible DUPLICATE/confusion source. No fills staged; nothing resolved (existence doubt blocks confident spec work).
